checks.diagnosis: The prompt routinely permits cuts that split a finite copula/auxiliary or main verb from the phrase that completes its core predicate, producing left fragments that contradict or lose the asserted meaning.
checks.evidence: en_us_721, en_us_378, en_us_399, en_us_1434, en_us_738 — each case shows a kept policy cut immediately after a finite copula/auxiliary or main verb while the offline target avoids cutting before the verb's required complement.
checks.type_predicate: a candidate cut that immediately follows a finite copular or auxiliary verb (e.g. is/are/was/were/has/have/does/did) and the next token begins a noun phrase, adjective phrase, or clause serving as that verb's complement

edit.text: Do not cut immediately after a finite copula/auxiliary or main verb when the continuation begins a complement (NP/AdjP/that-clause); such cuts leave a predicate fragment that reverses or contradicts the isolated left span.

orders.diagnosis: When several candidate cuts fall inside the same multiword noun phrase or coordinated NP, the prompt sometimes ranks a cut that fragments the NP above one that preserves the NP head; the safer choice is to preserve a grammatically complete NP on the left.
orders.evidence: en_us_998, en_us_334, en_us_121, en_us_1081 — in each sentence the measurement prefers preserving the multiword/coordinated NP intact, while the policy favored cuts that split the NP head from its modifiers.
orders.type_predicate: a configuration where both candidate cuts occur inside the same multiword noun phrase (including coordinated NPs or 'X of Y' constructions) in the same sentence

edit.text: When two cuts lie inside the same noun phrase, prefer the cut that leaves the left span a complete NP (includes the NP head) over the cut that fragments the NP.
